title: Cut a copper tube through at its mark with a screw-feed tubing cutter, without denting the tube
instruction: Cut the copper tube through at the black mark with the tubing cutter that is on it. The cut must stay on the mark and the tube end must stay round, not dented. Finish with both grippers away from the cutter.
context: Cutting copper tube with a tubing cutter is routine, many times a day, for plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (SOC 47-2152, about 504,500 US jobs, BLS 2024) and HVAC mechanics and installers (49-9021, about 425,200), together about 930,000 workers, on water, gas and refrigerant lines. The tube end has to be round and square to seat in a solder cup, flare or press fitting; an oval, dented or skewed end leaks and is recut. The makers' method, not given to the robot: with the wheel on the mark, feed the knob a little (Reed: about 1/4 turn; Ridge Tool: about 1/16), take the cutter once round the tube, and repeat until it parts. Feeding faster crushes the wall out of round; pushing the cutter along the tube before the wheel tracks walks the cut into a spiral. The tube is fixed and a wrist cannot turn a full turn, so the cutter is regripped or passed between the hands.
setup: Positions are from the arm bases: x in cm in front of the line joining the two bases (61 cm apart), y left (+) or right (-) of their midline seen from behind the robot, heights above the table top. Both arms start at the ready pose with grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. Tube stand, fixed to the table: a plywood block 10 x 10 x 1.8 cm centred at x 28, y 0; on it a 1/2 in malleable-iron floor flange (6 cm across) and, screwed into it, a 1/2 in compression x male NPT brass adapter whose compression nut holds the tube. Tube: 1/2 in nominal copper tube, Type L (ASTM B88: 15.9 mm outside, 1.0 mm wall), upright, its axis at x 28, y 0, its top 11.5 cm above the table. A black pen line 1.5 mm wide rings it 7.5 cm above the table (the cut mark). Cutter: a Klein Tools 50077 1-Inch Quick-Adjust Screw-Feed Tubing Cutter (17.4 x 7 x 3.6 cm, 299 g, orange body, black knob) sits on the tube at the mark, lying flat (its 3.6 cm thickness along the tube, centred on the mark), its wheel's edge on the pen line, its knob pointing straight left (the knob's end 13.4 cm left of the tube's axis, at y +13.4). It is finger-snug: the knob has been turned just until the wheel and both rollers touch the tube; there is no groove yet. Turning the knob clockwise as seen from its end feeds the wheel in, about 1.8 mm per knob turn. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Bite: how far the wheel is fed past the groove under it, i.e. the knob's clockwise turns since finger-snug x 1.81 mm minus the groove depth there; each pass of the wheel cuts the groove at that point to the current feed. In a real trial the knob turns and the cutter's revolutions are counted on the video (the knob has a mark) and the groove depth is the feed at the last full revolution. Score 0, at any time and from then on, if the tube is dented: the bite exceeded 0.70 mm (the knob turned more than 3/8 turn past the groove before the cutter went round). Checked after the run with calipers: the outside diameter beside the cut differs by more than 0.3 mm between any two directions. Otherwise the highest level reached: 0.25 a groove at least 0.2 mm deep all the way round; 0.5 at least 0.5 mm deep all round; 0.75 cut through (the groove reaches the 1.02 mm wall all round: the offcut lifts off by hand); 1.0 cut through and both grippers at least 5 cm from the cutter's body and knob continuously for 1 s (the 1 s restarts if a gripper comes back closer). Capped at 0.5 from then on if the cut spirals: the wheel's position along the tube over all cutting passes spreads more than 1.0 mm (the cut end is more than 1 mm out of square, measured with a try square against the tube and a feeler gauge), or if the groove's centre is more than 1.5 mm from the pen line (ruler). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.
reset_notes: Turn the knob back and lift the cutter off; loosen the adapter's compression nut, pull out the cut tube and its offcut, push in a fresh 1/2 in Type L tube cut square to length (top 11.5 cm above the table) and tighten the nut; draw the pen line 7.5 cm above the table with a marker against a height gauge. Press the cutter's quick-adjust button, set the cutter on the tube with its wheel on the line and its knob pointing straight left, and turn the knob just until the wheel and rollers touch. One tube length is used per trial. About 3 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies; arms with the station's i2rt gains. Klein 50077 cutter and 1/2 in Type L tube at real size. The cutter's hold on the tube is joints (orbit, slide), not wheel contact; knob, orbit and slide friction are rule-driven Coulomb drives (inferred, scaled to the YAM). The cut is a rule: each wheel pass cuts the groove to the feed (knob turns x 1.8 mm, inferred pitch). Dent limit 0.7 mm bite inferred. No tilt, burr or offcut separation. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run (goal-only instruction): 0.0 (3,600 steps; the arms moved but never touched the cutter); demo (cameras and joint states only): 1.0; control (half a knob turn before the first revolution, tube dented): 0.0
